title: We stopped writing design specs. Agents needed schemas.
excerpt: A design spec can guide a person and still leave an agent guessing. We moved the executable parts into JSON Schema. This is what changed.

title: Agents need a design-system runtime, not a component library
excerpt: A component library stores parts. An agent also needs rules, state, and a way to check its own output while it works.

title: What I mean by a generative design system
excerpt: The useful part is not generating endless components. It is giving the system enough structure to make a new interface without losing the product's rules.

title: A bigger prompt did not fix our design pipeline
excerpt: One agent kept mixing research, design, critique, and implementation. Splitting those jobs and routing the work made the system easier to trust.

title: Committee idea: Socratic Thread
excerpt: Four agents debated an AI tutor built around argument trees. The verdict: prove the interaction before spending time on the model.

title: Committee idea: Heartspace
excerpt: The committee looked at a workspace that responds to biometric signals. The idea survived, but only with tighter privacy and consent rules.

title: Your CSS Is Too Complex for AI Agents
excerpt: Agents make fewer mistakes when the stylesheet has clear tokens, predictable layers, and fewer ways to express the same decision.

title: What changed when I added agents to my design workflow
excerpt: A practical look at where agents helped, where they created more work, and which design decisions still needed me in the loop.

title: Why I start agent-ready design systems with tokens
excerpt: Tokens give people and agents the same vocabulary for color, type, spacing, and state. That shared vocabulary matters more than another component catalog.

title: AI design tools need more than a chat box
excerpt: Design work is spatial, persistent, and collaborative. I looked at what an AI tool would need if chat were only one part of the interface.
